answers.answer: All Restricted and Confidential data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 or an equivalent-strength algorithm approved by Security Engineering. This covers production databases and their read replicas, object storage (Amazon S3) used for customer data, staging, and exports, block storage volumes attached to production compute, backups and snapshots, and log storage. Encryption at rest is applied by default at the storage layer; engineers may not create production storage resources with encryption disabled, and automated configuration checks flag and block unencrypted resources. Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled before they are issued.

answers.answer: Yes. Every Tidewell-issued laptop must be enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system and have full-disk encryption enabled before it is issued and at all times afterward. IT keeps an inventory of all Tidewell-issued laptops that records each laptop's security status. Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically, and if they are not fixed within 3 days they lose access to corporate systems until they are compliant again.

citations.passage: Every Tidewell-issued laptop must meet the following before it is issued and at all times afterward:

| Device management | Enrolled in Tidewell's mobile device management (MDM) system |
| Full-disk encryption | Enabled |
IT maintains an inventory of all Tidewell-issued laptops, including the assigned user, model, serial number, and security status.
Laptops that fall out of compliance are flagged automatically. If not fixed within 3 days, the laptop loses access to corporate systems until it is compliant again.

answers.reasoning_note: Answered from the current Endpoint & Asset Management Standard (KB-27 v1.2, effective Feb 1, 2026). KB-07 §3.4 and KB-22 say the same thing, and so do the 2024 past answers (KB-32 A-058/A-059), which are lower authority.

No passage mentions a bug bounty or researcher rewards. Related: KB-16 §8 (v1.3) has a vulnerability disclosure process (security@tidewelldata.example, acknowledged within 3 business days), but that doesn't confirm or rule out a bounty.

No source says whether the full pentest report is shared under NDA. Related: Trust Center (KB-01) lists only a 'Penetration Test Summary Letter' as 'On request' (KB-17, Brightline, May 29, 2026); only the SOC 2 report is listed 'Under NDA'. A human should confirm the full-report policy.

No retrieved passage mentions a SOC or 24/7 coverage. Related: KB-06 v1.4 §7 says automated detection alerts go to the Security team's queue; KB-10 v2.0 §6.2 sets a 30-minute SEV1 triage target. Neither confirms or rules out 24/7 operation.

answers.answer: Under our current Information Security Policy (v3.2, effective February 1, 2026), the Head of Security owns the security program day to day, and the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is the accountable executive for the information security program. A Security & Compliance team implements and monitors security controls. Our documents do not name the person in this role and do not state how large the security team is.

answers.reasoning_note: Partial answer. KB-02 v3.2 covers who leads security by role, but no passage gives a CISO title, a person's name, or team headcount.
